speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There are several facilities in Singapore that require security protection.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The security measures required at these different facilities are assessed by the relevant agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Jurong Island and Changi Airport are among the facilities that are considered to be high risk.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Anyone who wishes to have access to the restricted areas in these facilities will have to be screened by the Police.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have seen in Singapore and overseas, incidents where insiders used or attempted to use their access for wrong purposes, sometimes with serious consequences.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Past offences are a consideration when screening persons for such passes.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: However, the Police do not rule out ex-offenders on a blanket basis.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The factors relating to the offence are assessed.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: A person with antecedents of concern may also be required to remain offence-free for some time, before he or she is allowed access into such sensitive facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Member may wish to clarify the specific categories of offences and the associated facilities that he thinks should be exempted from such screening, if that is the purport of his question.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I say this because it is not clear what the real concern is.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Is the concern that these people are not able to find decent jobs, or they are not able to find jobs in specific security-sensitive places?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Our approach is to help ex-offenders find decent jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Yellow Ribbon Singapore (YRSG) works closely with employers and industry partners, so that an ex-offender can find jobs across a wide range of sectors, and not just at key installations.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: As any employer will tell Members here, the key issue in Singapore is, actually, a lack of manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: YRSG provides employment assistance in three ways: placement services, career retention support and engagements with industry stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: On placement services, placement exercises are held in prison to match inmates with suitable employers.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The inmate's interests, skill level and incarceration history are considered, to best match them to a job.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In 2021, YRSG provided employment assistance to over 2,900 inmates.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But even after finding a job, some may face challenges transiting from prison to the work environment.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: YRSG assigns a Career Coach to each ex-offender at work for up to 12 months after their release.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Career Coaches engage ex-offenders regularly to set behavioural goals and provide encouragement and work closely with their employers to resolve work-related issues.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, I hope Members will appreciate that quite a lot is done to help them, because we want them to succeed.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Of the ex-offenders released in 2020, Career Retention Support was provided for more than 1,700 persons.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: As at December 2021, 87% had stayed on the job for three months and 70% for six months.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And I think, if you compare it across the world, our approach compares with the best around.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Third, YRSG actively engages industry and employers on good career opportunities available.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Earlier this year, I mentioned the TAP and Grow initiative to this House.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Under the TAP and Grow initiative, training academies in prison have been set up in partnership with the Media, Precision Engineering and Logistics sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Inmates will be offered jobs by partner employers upon release.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: About 650 inmates will benefit from the TAP and Grow initiative in these three sectors every year.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This year, YRSG aims to expand the initiative into the Food Services sector.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, both Mr Leon Perera and other Members can see, a lot of effort has been put into this, into helping ex-offenders find and keep decent jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is not clear to me why the focus is on employment of ex-offenders at key security installations specifically, without considering the wider landscape and the efforts by YRSG, which I am sure all Members are aware of.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Member's colleague, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, made a somewhat related set of points last year.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And I told him, do you want convicted paedophiles working in childcare centres?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Or those who have been convicted of serious offences, albeit non-violent – to use his language – to be security officers at condominiums?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Or would it be better that we have a risk matrix and assess suitability for different jobs and yet help all of them find jobs?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We take their livelihoods seriously and we want to help them.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I also suggested to Assoc Prof Jamus Lim that if he suggested some condominiums in suitable places, we can consider trying out his suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The proof of the suggestion and how serious it is, is in getting it done on the ground.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Since then, I have not heard from Assoc Prof Jamus Lim.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Likewise, if Mr Leon Perera thinks it is useful, he can suggest some condominiums to try out these ideas.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Then maybe we can take these suggestions seriously and not dismiss them as political soundbites.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, I will repeat my suggestion here: if Mr Leon Perera or Assoc Prof Jamus Lim believes that ex-offenders – be they child molesters or have convictions for housebreaking – should be allowed to be, say, security officers, without their conviction record being available to employers or that they should be allowed access to highly security-sensitive locations; first, maybe we can try out some private installations which they can suggest, and I am prepared to consider this favourably.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: By looking at this question, my view would be that a nuanced approach and a calibrated approach should be taken whereby the gravity of the offence and the length of time that the ex-offender has been offence-free be taken into consideration, rather than a blanket prohibition be imposed.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I think the Minister did confirm that that is the case – that a nuanced approach is taken.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And I appreciate the other efforts across the whole landscape that YRSG has been undertaking to help ex-offenders to re-integrate and find alternative employment.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My particular question was just in relation to those two facilities that are, of course, high-risk, we do recognise that, and with a view to ascertain that there is no blanket prohibition.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I think the Minister did confirm that is the case.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I feel that it is useful for me to clarify that the specific Parliamentary Question that I had posed last year mentioned, specifically, that it was with regard to non-violent offenders, of which, in a number of categorisations, including the UN, exclude sexual crimes and misdemeanours.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: So, I think it is a bit of a mischaracterisation to argue that it is about allowing paedophiles back into the system.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, would the Member consider those people to be suitable to be security officers?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Looking at pornography, child pornography is also non-violent.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Would the Member agree to such people acting as kindergarten teachers in registered kindergartens?
